messages:
anna: quick poll — compact Create Model flow: show 'Required' word, asterisk, or omit in dense rows? need direction before i push the figma update. lexi: prefer the literal word 'Required' in labels for dense views. asterisk-only is ambiguous for assistive tech. if space is tight, use visually condensed 'Req' token but ensure screen reader reads full word. jamal: +1 on tokenized label. for really cramped grids consider showing the marker only on the first column label and toggling an expanded view that shows 'Required' for each field. avoids clutter but keeps discoverability. mike: implementation note: make the token translatable and allow layout variants. also use a muted color token for the label so it's not visually heavy. sam: tiny accessibility nit — whatever we do, include the required state in the programmatic name, not just as decorative text. e.g., "". rachel: validation surfaces: inline messages for single-field errors; some teams want a pinned step summary bar for cross-field or policy validation. i'm leaning to providing both. lexi: agree — summary bar works well for multi-field rules. make it keyboard-focusable and include small link anchors that jump and focus each problem input. aria-live politely announcing the new summary is helpful so screen reader users notice it. anna: (typo: i'm anna — used earlier alias) — don't forget layout shift concerns. errors shouldn't push down the form. reserve an error/helper line under inputs and flip text/color when needed. mike: CSS suggestion for reserve: `.input-helper-line { min-height: 1.125rem; }` keeps layout stable while allowing longer helper copy. jamal: on destructive confirmations: alternatives include typed phrase (type MODEL_NAME), a required checkbox + CTA, or a two-step toast confirmation. which to choose for model deletion vs org purge? lexi: propose a scope-based rule: typed phrase (exact match) only for cluster/org-critical operations that impact billing or data retention; checkbox + clear copy for single-resource deletes; two-step toast for reversible non-critical actions. sam: mobile UX matters: typed phrase is painful on phones. reserve it for <10 operations that are extremely high-risk. otherwise checkbox is fine. mike: if we use typed phrase, make the input accessible — explicit label, not just placeholder, and announce mismatch errors with role=\"alert\". e.g., "
No match
". also provide a visible affordance for copying the exact string on mobile. rachel: curious about showing a top summary pinned to the form header vs a floating toast. pinned feels discoverable for multi-error flows; toast works for ephemeral notices. lexi: pinned summary is better with large forms because it stays in context. ensure it has links like "Replicas must be <= 100" and on click call `document.getElementById('replicas').focus()` so screen readers jump. anna: decision draft for the component patch: 1) required tokenized word in labels for dense variants (with optional condensed token), 2) inline field errors with reserved helper line and aria-invalid/aria-describedby, 3) pinned step summary for cross-field/policy issues with focusable anchors, 4) typed-phrase confirm only for org/cluster-critical ops; checkbox-confirm for resource deletes, 5) provide accessible typed-confirm examples (visible label + role=\"alert\") and copy/clipboard affordance on mobile. mike: i'll make a small demo repo and a frontend PR with dense vs expanded label variants, helper-line CSS, the pinned summary component, and a typed-confirm example (with a11y hooks). design-bot: created issue https://redwood.internals/issue/7301 — "forms: compact label variants + pinned summary + scoped confirmation patterns" :white_check_mark: anna: awesome — i'll update figma tokens and include the condensed token option. thanks all :thumbsup:
